newsitem.title: INDIA: UTI plans $150 mln offshore Indian debt fund.
newsitem.headline: UTI plans $150 mln offshore Indian debt fund.

text.p: Unit Trust of India (UTI) plans to launch a $150 million offshore debt fund, the country's first, by the end of April, the Business Standard daily reported on Friday.
UTI is in talks with Nomura International in London to handle the marketing of the fund to institutional investors in Europe, the United States and Far East.
The Mauritius based fund will be listed on the London Stock Exchange (LSE), and will invest mainly in corporate debt, not more than 10 percent will be invested in government paper.
"The scheme will be close-ended for the first three years and then turn open," the newspaper quoted a senior UTI official as saying.
He said Indian debt had a relatively long lock-in period and there was little depth in the secondary market, so the scheme was close-ended to start with to stop any sudden redemption pressure.
Any investors quitting the fund after three years will exit at the price quoted on the LSE.
"After three years, redemption will be at net asset value," the official said.
UTI chairman G.P. Gupta listed some of the fund's attractions.
"The stable rupee, current high interest rates, and capital appreciation arising out of the decline in interest rates are some of the key attractions of the fund," he said.
